models.label: G-score
models.description: Classic, but noisy categories (steals, percentages, turnovers) weigh less, because weekly results in them are closer to luck. Best match to our weekly H2H simulation (2026-10-13 research).

models.label: Z-score 9-cat
models.description: Classic. Each category: distance from the pool average in standard deviations. Sum of 9.

models.label: Punt z-score
models.description: Classic, with the categories you turn off removed.

models.label: Minus-1
models.description: Classic, without each player's own worst category. The value for a team that punts that category.

models.label: DURANT H2H (Lloyd)
models.description: Josh Lloyd's head-to-head list as he published it: skew-corrected categories (Yeo-Johnson), points weigh most (REB 0.94, AST 0.75, the rest 0.60), no turnovers, the player's worst category dropped. His list is per game with the pool set to all.

models.label: DURANT (Lloyd, all categories)
models.description: Lloyd's broad DURANT for roto and H2H: skew-corrected categories, all equal, turnovers at half weight. Per game, pool all.

models.label: Simulated H2H
models.description: Our own model: the player joins hundreds of random teams drawn from the top 144, every team plays every fantasy week on expected weekly lines (per game x games that week x availability). Value = category wins above 50% per 100 matchups. Totals basis counts games played; per game assumes every week played.

dollars.description: Value above replacement level. All drafted players share the league budget.
Like plain, but cheap players are worth less because waivers replace them. Stars get more.
